row.passage: Dried parsley should never be used in cooking, for it is far less tasty and healthful than fresh parsley is.
row.question: Which one of the following principles, if valid, most clearly helps to justify the argument above?
options: Fresh ingredients should be used in cooking whenever possible.
Ingredients that should never be used in cooking are generally neither tasty nor healthful.
Only the tastiest ingredients should ever be used in cooking.
Parsley that is not both tasty and healthful should never be used in cooking.

steps.title: All trie nodes, p_theta

steps.title: Call node_stats

steps.title: Call _split
steps.body: `node_stats` calls `_split`. Its arguments are on the right; the steps that follow run inside it, and this line is highlighted again when the call returns.

steps.title: Log-softmax over the whole vocabulary
steps.body: `node_stats` runs first, on p0. Log-probabilities over all V tokens, at every node.

steps.title: Keep only the illegal tokens
steps.body: Legal columns become -inf. What remains is the model's mass outside the trie. Its highest token is the model's favourite way to answer outside the format.

steps.title: Legal and illegal mass
steps.body: `log_m` is the log of the mass on legal tokens and `log_r` the log of the mass on illegal tokens, each by its own logsumexp. The illegal mass is summed directly, not computed as `1 - m`, which rounds to 0 in fp32 when the legal mass is nearly 1.

steps.title: Split p0 into legal and illegal
steps.body: `s` is the result of the `_split` call above: p0's log-probabilities, its illegal part and the two masses.

steps.title: p0's top illegal tokens
steps.body: Subtracting `log_r` renormalizes the illegal log-probabilities into a distribution over illegal tokens only. The top 64 (`TOP`) are kept: `idx` their ids, `lp` their log-probabilities. Only these enter the L_out anchor.

steps.title: The reference statistics
steps.body: p0's legal mass, illegal mass and top illegal tokens at every node. Computed without gradients and used as fixed targets.

steps.title: Call node_anchor
steps.body: `_loss_terms` calls `node_anchor`. Its arguments are on the right; the steps that follow run inside it, and this line is highlighted again when the call returns.

steps.title: The same split for p_theta
steps.body: This time with gradients. `s` holds p_theta's log-probabilities, illegal part and masses.

steps.title: L_mass per node
steps.body: A binary KL between p0 and p_theta over (legal, illegal): m0 (log m0 - log m) + r0 (log r0 - log r). Zero when training leaves the legal/illegal split of mass untouched.

steps.title: p_theta on p0's top illegal tokens
steps.body: p_theta's log-probabilities at the token ids in `ref['idx']`, renormalized by p_theta's own illegal mass. `[N, K]`, comparable with `ref['lp']`.

steps.title: Call _kl_top
steps.body: `node_anchor` calls `_kl_top`. Its arguments are on the right; the steps that follow run inside it, and this line is highlighted again when the call returns.

steps.title: The remainder bucket, p0
steps.body: The K tokens do not hold all the illegal mass. `log(1 - exp(logsumexp))` is the log-probability of everything else, a (K+1)-th bucket. `_log1mexp` clamps inside the log so the gradient stays finite when the top tokens hold all the mass.

steps.title: p0 over K + 1 buckets
steps.body: The top tokens plus the remainder.

steps.title: The remainder bucket, p_theta
steps.body: The same for p_theta.

steps.title: p_theta over K + 1 buckets
steps.body: Aligned bucket by bucket with p0.

steps.title: KL(p0 || p_theta)
steps.body: `sum(ref * (log ref - log mod))` over the K + 1 buckets: one value per node.

steps.title: Two per-node vectors
steps.body: `mass` is L_mass and `out` is L_out at each node, before weighting.

steps.title: Anchors at every node
steps.body: `anchor['mass']` and `anchor['out']`, each `[N]`. Each node is weighted by `weight` and summed below.

steps.title: The two L_pos positions
steps.body: The reply start (the position before `Best answer: [` begins) and the position after the closing `]`, stacked as `[2, V]`.

steps.title: The same under p0
steps.body: The reference logits at those two positions.

steps.title: Call tree_loss
steps.body: `_loss_terms` calls `tree_loss`. Its arguments are on the right; the steps that follow run inside it, and this line is highlighted again when the call returns.

steps.title: L_tree: gold-path logits
steps.body: `_loss_terms` passes `cur_path` (`[T, V]`), the first T rows of `legal`, and the gold ids.

steps.title: Normalizer over legal tokens
steps.body: Illegal logits are set to -inf, so each node's `lse` is the log of the sum of exp(logit) over the legal tokens only. The full-vocabulary normalizer cancels in the loss.

steps.title: L_tree
steps.body: `lse - z[gold]` is -log of the gold token's probability renormalized over the legal tokens, at each node. Summed over the path it is -log of the product: the probability of the whole gold answer under the trie (Eq. 2).

steps.title: Call pos_stats
steps.body: `_loss_terms` calls `pos_stats`. Its arguments are on the right; the steps that follow run inside it, and this line is highlighted again when the call returns.

steps.title: p0's top tokens at the two sites
steps.body: For L_pos the sites have no trie, so the anchor is on the model's top 64 tokens overall.

steps.title: Call pos_anchor
steps.body: `_loss_terms` calls `pos_anchor`. Its arguments are on the right; the steps that follow run inside it, and this line is highlighted again when the call returns.

steps.title: p_theta at those tokens
steps.body: p_theta's log-probabilities at p0's top tokens, for each site.

steps.title: KL per site
steps.body: The same top-K-plus-remainder KL as before, one value per site. `_loss_terms` sums the two and multiplies by 0.5.

steps.title: Four scalars
steps.body: [L_tree, L_mass, L_out, L_pos]. L_tree sums over the path; L_mass and L_out are the `weight`-weighted sums of the per-node vectors; L_pos is 0.5 times the sum over its two sites.

steps.title: Back in compute
steps.body: The four scalars come back as separate tensors.
